narrative:
The model determined that you have a 26% chance of being a bad credit risk. While this is not an extremely high probability, it was enough for the bank to deny your loan application.

The three factors that mattered most in this decision were your other debtors or guarantors, the length of the loan you requested, and the status of your checking account. Having a guarantor was the strongest influence, and in your case it actually worked in your favor by pushing the prediction toward good credit. Most approved applicants have no guarantor at all, so the bank viewed your guarantor as a positive safety net.

The requested loan duration of 12 months was the second most important factor and also helped your case. Approved applicants typically request almost 20 months on average, so your shorter timeframe reduced the bank's perceived risk.

Unfortunately, the status of your checking account worked against you and ultimately tipped the decision toward denial. Your account being in negative balance (<0 DM) is relatively uncommon. Only about 13% of applicants are in this situation, while the majority of approved loans go to people with no checking account or positive balances. This negative status was the main reason the model saw elevated risk.

To improve your chances next time, focus on bringing your checking account balance into positive territory before reapplying. You may also want to consider requesting a slightly longer loan term if it better fits your needs, as shorter durations are viewed more favorably. Consider speaking with a financial advisor about steps to strengthen your overall credit profile.
